evidence: Block has four levels ('an ordered factor with levels 4 < 2 < 3 < 1'), too few for a grouping factor, and variety is the treatment; each of the 224 plots (latitude, longitude) holds one row, and Pinheiro and Bates (2000, sec. 5.3) fit gls(yield ~ variety - 1) with a spatial correlation and no block effect.

One row per worker of the May 1985 CPS ('Cross-section data'); region has two levels ('Does the individual live in the South?') and ethnicity, occupation and sector are few-level classes of the page's lm(log(wage) ~ ...) fits.

One row per man of the March 1988 CPS ('Cross-section data'); region holds the four census regions, a covariate of the page's Buchinsky lm and rq fits (region*smsa), and no column indexes a unit the men repeat within.
One row per worker aged 21-64 of the 2004 March CPS; region has four levels ('Northeast', 'Midwest', 'South', 'West'), a design factor, and no column indexes a unit the workers repeat within.
One row per worker of two March CPS cross sections ('the distribution of earnings in the US in 1992 and 2004'); year has two levels, a design factor, and no worker repeats.
One row per worker of two March CPS cross sections, 1992 and 1998; year has two levels, a design factor, and no worker repeats.

One row per High School and Beyond student ('students from approximately 1,100 high schools') with no school, county or state column; unemp ('county unemployment rate'), wage and tuition ('state' values) are merged area attributes (openml_378), region has two levels ('West or other'), and the page fits no model.

One row per credit card applicant ('Cross-section data'); months ('Months living at current address'), reports and active are counts, and Greene's (2003) fits are lm, Poisson, logit and zero-inflated models with no grouping.

year ('GSS year for respondent') is the survey wave, eight waves 1974-2002 ('every fourth year') of 767-1688 women each, but the page's probit, Poisson and negative binomial fits (Winkelmann and Boes 2009, Examples 3.14 and 8.11) enter it as a fixed linear trend, year - 1974, so the table keeps its filing (GSSvocab).
One row per person of the 1996 Medical Expenditure Panel Survey ('Cross-section data'); family is the family size, region has four levels, and the page only tabulates selfemp by insurance.

One row per Medicaid eligible ('Cross-section data'), the two sites ('Santa Barbara and Ventura counties') held by no column; school counts years of school, program has two levels, and Gurmu (1997) fits Poisson, negative binomial and hurdle models per program.

One row per household ('Cross-section data about fixed versus adjustable mortgages for 78 households'); school and years are counts, and no column identifies a household or lender; the page only plots rate.
One row per state in 1950 ('Cross-section data on states'); time is the 'Median time served (in months)', a covariate of Maddala's lm, logit and probit fits.

One row per student with kindergarten to grade 3 as columns (readk to read3, mathk to math3, stark to star3, schoolidk to schoolid3); the page reshapes it long by grade and fits lm(I(read + math) ~ 0 + grade/star), and the long form is in the registry as mlmRev star and rabe_hesketh star1.dta.

One row per ACLED country with population and GDP per capita per year as columns (pop2020 to pop2023, GDPpcn2020 to GDPpcn2023, GDPpcp2020 to GDPpcp2023) and their means; a lookup table 'created to facilitate merging', with no model.

Each row is a cell of income class and household size (pct, the 'cellule weight') in one year of 1973-1992, so year, income and size classify aggregate cells rather than index sampled units (hand check #162; as ordinal's income, one distribution per year); Bollino, Perali and Rossi (2000) fit a demand system with no random term.
One row per worker ('observation: individuals'); year ('survey year') holds four waves, 1992 to 1998, too few for a grouping factor, and sex two levels (Stock and Watson 2003, chapter 3).
One row per person ('a cross-section from 1986', 'observation: individuals'); doctor is 'the number of doctor visits', the count response, and no column indexes a unit.

One row per young man with the first observation and 1980 as paired columns (rns/rns80, mrt/mrt80, smsa/smsa80, age/age80, school/school80, expr/expr80, tenure/tenure80, lw/lw80); year is the first observation's year.
One row per wife ('a cross-section from 1993') with a sampling weight wght; region has four levels ('other, northcentral, south, west'), and no column indexes a unit the wives repeat within.
One row per respondent of the contingent valuation survey ('observation: individuals'); schooling is years of schooling and the 1-5 attitude items are covariates, no column indexes a unit.

One row per individual of the RAND Health Insurance Experiment (Deb and Trivedi 2002); family members share linc, lfam and educdec ('years of schooling of household head'), but no person or family column indexes them (openml_378).
One row per Belgian household ('a cross-section from 1995-96'); region has three exhaustive levels (flanders, wallon, brussels), a design factor, and occupation three.
One row per worker with exper, sex, school and wage and no id or year column; the page's 'panel of 595 observations from 1976 to 1982' is copied from Wages and indexes nothing in this table.

One row per year 1800-2010 and one column per country ('The remaining columns carry the names of the countries'), each the country's yearly crisis indicator, so the countries' repeated measures are stored as columns.
One row per nuclear-weapon state ('Data on the 9 nuclear-weapon states as of April 2019'), the columns its attributes; no unit repeats.
One row per respondent, id an 'identifier' held once; ratemarr is a 1-5 marriage rating, a covariate, and the notes suggest linear, Poisson, probit or logit models of naffairs or affair.

One row per individual (Terza 2002); unemrate ('state unemployment rate'), beertax, cigtax and ethanol are merged state attributes, but no column names the state and region is three dummies (openml_378).
One row per game between natural rivals ('Michigan-Michigan State, California-Stanford'), each pair once, coded as home-minus-visitor differences (dscore, dinstt, dapps); no school column repeats.
One row per audit pair, the white and the black tester's outcomes as the columns w ('white app. got job offer') and b ('black app. got job offer'), y = b - w their difference.

Cities in 1982 and 1987 ('year: 82 or 87', d87) with no city column ('Unfortunately, I do not have the list of cities'); Heiss builds the panel index from row order, so the replication has no replicate column (faraway rats), and year has two levels.
Each restaurant's first and second waves are columns (psoda/psoda2 to emp/emp2, '1st wave', '2nd wave'); the wide rule holds although county ('county label') groups the restaurants (hand check #162).

year ('72 to 84, even') is the GSS survey wave, seven waves of 142-186 women each, but Wooldridge's Example 13.1 (Used in Text: pages 449-450) fits it fixed with the dummies y74 to y84 the table holds, so the table keeps its filing (GSSvocab).

One row per woman of Botswana's 1988 Demographic and Health Survey; yearborn, monthfm and yearfm are birth and marriage dates and ceb and children counts, and no column indexes a unit (Computer Exercise C15.2).

year ('gss year for this respondent') is the GSS survey wave, seven waves 1994-2006 of 1337-2986 respondents each, which Wooldridge's exercises on HAPPINESS (C13.15 and its Chapter 17 sequel) fit fixed ('include a full set of year dummies', the y94 to y06 columns the table holds); region ('region of interview') holds the nine census divisions, a design factor, so the table keeps its filing (GSSvocab).

One row per injured worker in Kentucky or Michigan before or after the benefit change (afchnge, ky, mi), no worker repeating; indust and injtype are few-level classes and injdes a '4 digit injury description' code that classifies, and Example 13.4 fits the difference in differences by OLS.

One row per house sale ('year: 1978 or 1981'), no house repeating; nbh ('neighborhood, 1-6', with 0) is a handful of one town's neighborhoods, a design factor, and Example 13.3 fits the difference in differences by OLS.

One row per Boston mortgage application (Munnell et al. 1996); msa ('msa number of property') holds one value, unit is the 'number of units in property', and the text fits linear probability, logit and probit models of approve.

One row per player of the 1993 season; the team enters only through teamsal ('team payroll') and the city columns, with no team column, and the text fits OLS salary equations. RULE GAP: teamsal takes one value per team, constant over 9-15 players each, so it stands in for a team id, which openml_378's ruling on merged unit attributes leaves uncounted.
One row per NBA player of 1994-95; center is a position dummy ('=1 if center'), draft a draft number, and no team or season column repeats; the text fits OLS wage equations.
One row per person, case an 'identifier' held once (Biddle and Hamermesh 1990); yngkid is a child indicator and the rest are individual times and attributes.

One row per person with 1975 and 1981 as paired columns (slpnap75/slpnap81, totwrk75/totwrk81, educ75/educ81, marr75/marr81, gdhlth75/gdhlth81, yngkid75/yngkid81) and their changes (cslpnap, ctotwrk, cyngkid), the first differences of the text's pages 463-464.

One row per state with 1985 and 1990 as paired columns (dthrte85/dthrte90, open85/open90, admn85/admn90, speed85/speed90) and their changes; the package vignette's DD_model regresses cdthrte on copen and cadmn.

One row per congressional district with the 1988 and 1990 elections as paired columns (vote88/vote90, inexp88/inexp90, chexp88/chexp90, incshr88/incshr90) and their changes ('panel data, at the Congressional district level'); state also groups the districts.

One row per firm (cusip) with ten years as columns (pat70 to pat79, logr70 to logr79); Cameron and Trivedi's section 23.3 reshapes it long and fits a panel Poisson on the firm, and the 1975-1979 long form is in the registry as rabe_hesketh patents.dta (Ecdat PatentsHGH).
